correctness.rationale: Exact balance cancels second moments to q=A; fixed-point feedback follows by algebra. Weighted Chebyshev proves q>=T. A probability-measure maximizer exists and its first variation forces support only at spectral endpoints because the derivative numerator of h is strictly increasing. The resulting one-variable rational optimization yields the precise factor, rational-square-root finite equality criterion and general sharp approximations. Exact-rational testing of 32059 samples and stationary witnesses is supplementary, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The precise worst-case cost of the proposed computable descent certificate is a motivated missing quantity. Even in the strongest natural expected-feedback balance, the surrogate can lose a factor asymptotic to the full preconditioner condition number; explicit multiplicities identify why. This quantifies a material limitation in an optimization-relevant sufficient learning-rate rule, independently of algorithmic acceleration claims.
